newsitem.title: USA: National Semi plans $200 Web TV/NC chip.
newsitem.headline: National Semi plans $200 Web TV/NC chip.

text.p: National Semiconductor Corp unveiled Monday its design for a new microprocessor for use in Web TV browsers and Internet-based network computers, priced at under $200 per chip.

National said the new design, code-named "Odin," is a 486-based chip to be built around National's NS486SXF embedded processor for use in home TV Web browsers and low-cost network computers connected to central machines running Microsoft Corp's Windows NT.
The "Odin" reference design will be available to computer makers and software developers in the first quarter of 1997.

It said the "Odin" design includes a Trident Microsystems Inc graphics controller for an SVGA monitor and TV-quality picture and a Rockwell International Corp chip for a compact-disc quality audio system and a 33.6 kilobit per second modem connection.

The company said the chip incorporates all the features required to implement Web browsers or network computers including compatability with Sun Microsystems Inc's Java, PC-based keyboards, pointing devices and printers and standard Personal Computer Memory Card Industry Association (PCMCIA) expansion cards.
National said its design would work with a variety of operating systems and application programs.

Software vendors who are developing Internet software for the "Odin" platform include: Integrated Systems Inc, Javasoft (Sun), Magic Web, Microtec, Microware Systems Corp, QNX, Wind River Systems and others.
Because the NS486 runs on Java software, any Java-based application will also run on an "Odin" system, the chipmaker said.
